# Player ALAC goldens

Independent fixtures for the bridge player's ALAC decoder (backlog B470,
PR 1c).

Generated by `scripts/player-alac-goldens/generate.py`, which needs macOS
`afconvert` (Apple's ALAC encoder and decoder) and the Python standard
library. Ordinary `go test` never runs that script.

The expected audio is an integer pattern specified in the generator
(`pattern()`), which `alac_golden_test.go` reproduces and checks against the
manifest's `samples_sha256` before it compares a decode with it sample for
sample. Every encode was decoded back by `afconvert` and compared with the
pattern before it was written. The generator zeroes the creation and
modification times `afconvert` stamps into `mvhd`, `tkhd` and `mdhd`, so a
rerun leaves these files byte-identical.

To check a change to the generator without touching these files, write into
a scratch directory and point the golden tests at it:

```sh
python3 scripts/player-alac-goldens/generate.py --out DIR --codex EVALDIR
go test ./internal/player/decode -args -alac-goldens=DIR
```

The pattern changes kind every 1499 frames, so each 4096-frame packet holds
parts of several: only the low bits moving, signed extrema out of step,
full-scale noise, smooth triangle waves, correlated stereo, silence with one
impulse per channel, values next to the extrema with noise in the low byte,
and a one-step square beside a ramp. Left and right differ in every kind but
the silence. `afconvert` codes the packet that holds most of the noise as an
escape (uncompressed) packet and most of the others compressed, so each
fixture decodes both kinds; `TestALACGoldensDecodeBothPacketKinds` reads the
packet headers to keep it so.

| File | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `afconvert_16bit_44100.m4a` | 16-bit; `ftyp`, `moov`, a `free` box, then `mdat`; one chunk, no edit list; a 137-frame final packet |
| `afconvert_24bit_96000.m4a` | 24-bit at 96 kHz; the sample entry's 16-bit, 44.1 kHz fields are `afconvert`'s constants, not the stream's |
| `afconvert_24bit_192000.m4a` | 24-bit at 192 kHz; a final packet of one frame |
| `afconvert_32bit_44100.m4a` | 32-bit; a final packet one frame short of a whole one |
| `afconvert_24bit_96000_co64_moov_last.m4a` | The 96 kHz audio, unchanged, with `moov` after `mdat` and the chunk offsets in `co64` |
| `afconvert_16bit_44100_edit.m4a` | The 16-bit audio, unchanged, with an edit list: media time 123, 251 at a movie timescale of 1000, which is 11069.1 frames at 44.1 kHz, of which the 11069 covered whole are presented; `afconvert`'s own decode presents the same frames |
| `afconvert_20bit_48000.m4a` | Refused: `unsupported_bit_depth` (a real 20-bit ALAC, `afconvert -d alac/2`) |
| `afconvert_mono_44100.m4a` | Refused: `unsupported_channel_count` |
| `afconvert_aac_44100.m4a` | Refused: `lossy_refused` (AAC in M4A) |
| `ffmpeg_16b-44100hz-2ch-ffmpeg.m4a` | FFmpeg's ALAC encoder and muxer (Lavf63.1.102): `mdat` before `moov`, an edit list over the whole media, `maxRun` 0. From Codex's B470 ALAC evaluation (`generated/16b-44100hz-2ch-ffmpeg.m4a`); expected audio is the SHA-256 of the PCM Codex encoded |
| `ffmpeg_variant-edit123.m4a` | The same evaluation's `generated/variant-edit123.m4a`: an FFmpeg 24-bit, 48 kHz encode whose edit's media time Codex set to 123; the edit runs past the media's end, so 28686 frames are presented, as FFmpeg presents them |
